# Genesis Apocryphon Column 19 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 19 | **Condition:** Well preserved; major sections legible

---

**19:1** Then I, Abram, traveled through the land, along its length and its breadth, and I went about looking at it.

**19:2** I journeyed from the river Gihon to the shore of the sea, and I went along the Great Sea

**19:3** until I reached the mountain of Taurus. And I traveled from the shore of this great salt sea

**19:4** and went along the mountain of Taurus eastward through the breadth of the land

**19:5** until I reached the river Euphrates. And I journeyed along the Euphrates until I came to the Red Sea in the east.

**19:6** And I went along the Red Sea until I reached the tongue of the Sea of Reeds.

**19:7** And God said to me: To you I shall give all this land, and to your seed after you I shall give it;

**19:8** they shall possess it forever. And I shall multiply your seed as the dust of the earth

**19:9** which no man can number. Your seed also shall not be numbered.

**19:10** Arise, walk about in it, along its length and its breadth, and look, for to you I shall give it.

**19:11** Then I, Abram, went to dwell by the oaks of Mamre, which is in Hebron.

**19:12** And I built an altar there and offered upon it a burnt offering and a grain offering

**19:13** to God Most High. And I ate and drank there, I and all the men of my household.

**19:14** And I sent and invited Mamre, Ornam, and Eshkol, the three Amorite brothers, my friends, and they ate together with me.

**19:15** Before these days a famine came upon all the land. And I, Abram, went down to Egypt

**19:16** and entered Egypt. And I dwelt in the land of Egypt five years before my wife was taken from me.

**19:17** Now the king of Zoan gave to us much grain, and much oil, and much wine,

**19:18** and I had a dream. In my dream I saw a cedar tree and a palm tree growing from one root.

**19:19** Men came and sought to cut down the cedar tree and to leave the palm tree by itself.

**19:20** But the palm tree cried out and said: Do not cut down the cedar, for we are both from one root.

**19:21** And the cedar was spared on account of the palm tree.

**19:22** I awoke from my sleep in the night and said to Sarai my wife:

**19:23** I had a dream, and I am fearful on account of this dream. She said to me: Tell me your dream.

**19:24** And I told her, and she understood its meaning, and she said to me:

**19:25** They will seek to kill you and to spare me. This alone is the mercy which you must do for me:

**19:26** in every place where we come, say of me: She is my sister. And I shall live on account of you,

**19:27** and my life shall be saved because of you.

**19:28** And Abram wept on account of Sarai his wife that night, weeping bitterly.

**19:29** And I prayed that night, and I entreated, and I asked, and I said in my grief:

**19:30** Blessed are You, O God Most High, my Lord, over all the ages.

**19:31** For You are Lord and Master over all, and over all the kings of the earth You rule,

**19:32** to execute judgment upon them all. Now I make my complaint before You

**19:33** against Pharaoh Zoan, king of Egypt, because my wife has been taken from me by force.

**19:34** Execute judgment upon him for me, and show forth Your mighty hand against him and against all his house.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 19 is well preserved. This first-person narrative presents Abram's journey through the promised land, the famous cedar-and-palm dream, and the descent into Egypt. "Taurus" is used for tur tora (the mountain of the Bull) as the geographical identification. Note 19:25 — the original has Sarai understanding the dream as a threat to Abram's life, not her own; the pronouns reflect the dream's symbolism where the cedar (Abram) is threatened. "God Most High" renders El 'Elyon consistently.*
